tests_notes: Empty and single lists, found and missing pairs, no reuse of one position, equal numbers, negatives; workload: 800 numbers, one miss and one late hit.

A.strategy: One pass with a set of complements
A.rationale: Instead of trying all O(n²) pairs, remember the numbers seen so far in a set and test target - x in O(1). Returns True exactly when some pair sums to target.

B.strategy: Sort, then walk two pointers inward
B.rationale: After sorting, a pair summing to target exists iff two pointers moving inward meet it: O(n log n) instead of O(n²). Same boolean result for every input.

C.rationale: Conservative micro-optimization: computes len(numbers) once and target - numbers[i] once per outer step, so the inner loop is a single comparison. Same pairs visited in the same order.

A.diagnosis: Adding x to the set before the lookup let a number pair with itself: target 2 matched 1 + 1 in [3, 8, 1, 4]. Look up first, then add.
A.rationale: Each number is compared only with numbers at earlier positions, so one position is never used twice, while equal numbers at two positions still pair. O(n) instead of O(n²).

B.diagnosis: numbers.sort() reordered the caller's list in place; the original never modifies its argument. Sort a copy instead.
B.strategy: Two pointers over a sorted copy
B.rationale: sorted() leaves the caller's list untouched; walking two pointers inward over the copy finds a pair iff one exists, in O(n log n) instead of O(n²).

notes: Both fast ideas fail first: A lets a number pair with itself (a test catches it), B sorts the caller's list (only the differential check catches it). Both repairs win; C is a modest win.
